title: Scalable seed palette and type-scale mapping for high-contrast mode
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a deterministic, scalable mapping from Redwood's seed color palette and typographic scale to a high-contrast theme variant. Deliver token aliases, migration guidance for components (buttons, tables, charts), and a lightweight runtime-friendly interpolation strategy for client and server rendering. This ticket covers research, token definition, migration docs, and a small audit-run against the Console surface.
design_notes: Goal: support WCAG AA/AAA where feasible without breaking current visual language.
Prefer additive token aliases (e.g., color.fn.surface-contrast) rather than replacing base tokens to ease rollout.
High-contrast mapping should be reversible so customers can opt out of automated transforms.
Maintain proportional typographic relationships rather than absolute jumps to preserve layout stability.
Plan both static (build-time) and dynamic (runtime CSS variables) delivery modes depending on deployment (Hosted vs Private).
decisions: Use a seed-based HSL ramp with contrast-aware anchors instead of hand-crafted swatches to reduce maintenance overhead.
Typographic scale adjustments: prefer 100-150ms perceptual step increases for 'compact' controls; implement as delta tokens (type.delta.-1|0|+1) to avoid mass component changes.
Elevation/shadow: reduce subtle shadows in high-contrast mode and rely on strong edge separation (stroke tokens) for tables and dense lists.
Introduce 'contrast-fallback' token layer that falls back to nearest accessible token when computed contrast < target.
Deliver migration as additive token file and codemod snippets for component classnames/props.
Keep default tokens unchanged; high-contrast tokens live under tokens.high_contrast.* and map into component styles via token-bridge.
Accessibility review required before merge (include design + accessibility engineer).

acceptance_criteria: Token spec checked into design tokens repo as tokens.high_contrast.* and annotated with rationale.
Contrast validator script exists and reports no failing pairs for primary surfaces at target WCAG levels specified in the spec.
Button, Table, and Chart components render with high_contrast tokens behind a feature flag and don't shift layout by >8px at standard breakpoints.
Migration docs and codemod published with at least one example PR applying token aliases to an existing Console page.
Accessibility engineer sign-off recorded in comments and a follow-up ENG issue created for any residual engineering fixes.
Performance: runtime token switch using CSS variables must not add >2% to initial render critical path in Hosted Console benchmark.
